title: The Afternoon Brief: Cutdown day reshapes rosters; Ohtani's return stalls
dek: NFL teams finalized their 53-man rosters ahead of Sunday's 6 p.m. ET deadline, with trades and injury updates dominating the day, while Shohei Ohtani's pitching timeline extended again and Pete Crow-Armstrong's three-homer performance intensified the MVP race.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The NFL's roster cutdown produced significant player movement on the final deadline day, while baseball's injury and performance narratives shifted: Ohtani's return remains uncertain, Crow-Armstrong's late-season surge challenges Ohtani's MVP dominance, and the Red Sox added depth for the stretch run.
bottom_line: NFL rosters finalized by the 6 p.m. ET deadline on August 30, with notable trades reshaping depth at cornerback and interior line; Keenan Allen's DWI arrest early Sunday raises immediate questions about the Colts' receiver depth and league discipline. Ohtani's pitching timeline remains unclear after Roberts withheld him Sunday; Crow-Armstrong's three-homer game on August 29 tightened the NL MVP race against Ohtani's recent dominance. Watch the Colts' handling of Allen's situation and any NFL Personal Conduct review, Ohtani's next scheduled appearance or revised recovery update, and whether Crow-Armstrong sustains his late-season surge through September.
body: The NFL's August 30 cutdown deadline produced a series of high-profile trades and signings resolved just before the 6 p.m. ET gate closed. The Bears traded defensive tackle Gervon Dexter, a 2023 second-round pick who started all 19 games last season, to the Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick. The Bills sent center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, a 2024 fifth-round pick with 31 regular-season appearances, to the Colts in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick (the Bills gave up a seventh-rounder). Both moves point to teams reprioritizing depth at specific positions as rosters took final shape for Week 1.

A separate storm broke around Indianapolis Colts receiver Keenan Allen hours after the roster gate closed. Allen, 34, was arrested early Sunday morning on preliminary charges of DWI and DWI endangering a person, both misdemeanors, with a blood alcohol content of 0.08 or more, per Indianapolis Metro Police. The arrest occurred approximately 1 a.m. in downtown Indianapolis, roughly 12 hours after Allen caught one pass for 24 yards in Saturday's preseason game against Detroit. Allen signed a one-year deal with the Colts on August 19 that could reach $8.32 million. The arrest surfaces immediate questions about the team's roster decision and whether the NFL initiates a Personal Conduct Policy review.

On the baseball side, Shohei Ohtani's pitching return timeline stalled again. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced Ohtani will not pitch Sunday following continued soreness, stating Ohtani is "not 100%" per MLB.com. The team still expects his return as a pitcher this season, though no revised timeline has been provided. The delay extends a recovery window already extended past earlier targets.

In sharper contrast, Pete Crow-Armstrong's three-home-run performance on August 29 in the Cubs' 17-5 victory over Cincinnati intensified the National League MVP race. Crow-Armstrong hit half of Chicago's six home runs in the game, with announcer Boog Sciambi noting the season represented "an MVP type season." Crow-Armstrong faces Shohei Ohtani in voting, with Ohtani holding four MVP awards in the past five seasons. After the game, Crow-Armstrong attributed the performance to a prediction from Cubs legend Sammy Sosa: "Sammy did say I was gonna hit three today." The Red Sox added offensive depth by activating Roman Anthony and Trevor Story from the injured list ahead of Sunday's series finale against the Yankees; both players were immediately inserted into the starting lineup after missing more than three months. Arizona's JJ Wetherholt, a National League Rookie of the Year candidate, was placed on the injured list with right wrist tendinitis after playing through discomfort for weeks.

The day's through-line is one of roster finality meeting competitive uncertainty. Cutdown decisions locked in starting lineups and depth charts for the regular season, yet ongoing investigations, injury delays, and late-month performances are still reshaping what those rosters will accomplish. The Colts face an immediate credibility test around Allen's status; the Dodgers face a pitching depth question if Ohtani's return extends further; and baseball's MVP conversation has tightened enough that individual performances in September will matter.
